Docket 1.3.93

**Three findings that misread how institutions build their sites.**

- *"Pages canonicalise to a different URL … will not rank on its own" when the
  canonical is the page itself.* A canonical that names the page's own address
  by its index file — /about/index for /about/ — and redirects straight back
  is not handing the page's ranking away. It now gets its own, smaller finding:
  the tag points at a redirect, and should name the address that serves the
  page.
- *"Different phone numbers appear across the site" from a staff directory.* A
  page that lists who to call — departments, offices, the help desk — carries
  different numbers on purpose. Numbers that appear only on such a page no
  longer count as variants of one line.
- *"Promises one thing in search and another on the page" for a homepage
  titled with your name.* A title that is just your name promises your name; a
  slogan in the headline beneath it is not a mismatch. Titles that promise
  something specific still have to match their headline.

99 checks across 13 areas.
